newsitem.title: INDIA: Group wants zoo elephants unshackled in Bombay.
newsitem.headline: Group wants zoo elephants unshackled in Bombay.

text.p: An animal rights group wants three elephants shackled in concrete cubicles in a city-run zoo to be freed.
Ahimsa, or Non-Violence, said it launched a poster and signature campaign on behalf of the pachyderms.

"Chained and imprisoned for life in barren concrete, a far cry from their jungle home, without family -- Anarkali, Radha and Lakshmi -- elephants in the Bombay zoo, lead miserable deprived lives, driving them to insanity," the group said in a statement.
They said the zoo had not provided minimum living standards for the elephants three years after India's Central Zoo Authority gave the city a year's deadline to do so.
Ahimsa said the regulations require the animals be kept in their natural surroundings, be given 24-hour water, and a separate cubicle where they can rest.
By contrast, it said, "They are kept tied down with chains in three barren concrete cubicles that give them no movement, no privacy and no social contact with one another."
Zoo officials defended the arrangements and said they were meant to be temporary.
"We cannot risk visitors' lives, so the elephants are kept chained only for a certain number of hours every day," zoo Superintendent K.L. Velodi said.

"As to the enclosures, we have drawn up a five-million-rupee ($139,470) plan to build a new one. I expect work to begin on it within six months' time, after we get permission from the city administration."
Ahimsa said if demands to free the pachyderms are not met, the zoo should be closed.
